name: Triveni Sangam

caption: Triveni Sangam viewed from above, where the Ganga, Yamuna and mythical Saraswati are traditionally believed to meet.

Around thirty traditional wooden rowing boats with low canvas canopies, different sizes and slightly different colours, some tied in clusters near the point, a few moving, with small groups of pilgrims aboard, figures tiny and indistinct. Shot from 140 m above the Ganga, camera tilted 35° downward, 28mm full-frame perspective. Early winter morning, low sun from the right raking across the water and giving each boat a long soft shadow, thin river mist lifting off the surface, pale hazy sky. name: Jaisalmer Fort
alt: Aerial view of Jaisalmer Fort in Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, India
caption: Jaisalmer Fort, the 'Golden Fort', is one of the world's few living forts, with homes, shops and temples still inside its sandstone walls.
tags: India; Rajasthan; Jaisalmer; Jaisalmer Fort; Sonar Qila; Thar Desert; Hill Forts of Rajasthan; Aerial Photography; Drone Photography
prompt: Aerial photograph of Jaisalmer Fort (Sonar Qila) crowning Trikuta Hill above the town of Jaisalmer in the Thar Desert, Rajasthan. A long fortified wall of rough-hewn, dry-laid sandstone blocks follows the rim of the hill, with many rounded drum-shaped bastions along it; the stone is weathered, with pale streaks, chipped edges, darker staining below the parapets and patches of crumbling plaster. Inside the walls the whole hilltop is a tightly packed living settlement of flat-roofed sandstone houses at many levels, carved havelis with jharokha balconies, narrow lanes, rooftop water tanks, satellite dishes and drying laundry, with a few small stone temple spires rising from a flat horizontal skyline. Shot from 120 m above and south-west of the hill, camera tilted 30° downward, 32mm full-frame perspective. Below the fort the town of low flat-roofed buildings in pale straw-yellow sandstone and sun-faded plaster, each with different heights, window styles and rooftop clutter, a curving road with a few cars, motorcycles and one bus, sparse khejri trees, dry stony slopes with boulders, then flat open desert to a hazy horizon. Late afternoon, low sun from the left, long shadows between the bastions, visible stone grain and weathering, the stone a soft pale straw-yellow. Dry air with fine desert haze and a pale muted sky. Fort filling the left two-thirds, open hazy sky across the top. name: Pangong Lake
alt: Aerial view of Pangong Lake in Ladakh, India
caption: Pangong Lake, at about 4,200 m in Ladakh, shifts through shades of blue and stretches across the border into Tibet.
tags: India; Ladakh; Pangong Lake; Pangong Tso; Himalayas; High-altitude Lake; Aerial Photography; Drone Photography

The water lies in distinct bands: pale green-turquoise over pebbly shallows with the lake bed visible, shifting to deep blue further out, with fine wind ripples and a thin line of wave wash on the gravel shore. Rugged, angular mountain ridges of grey, brown and rust-coloured rock with visible strata, broken rock faces, scree slopes and talus fans and dry gullies; no sand dunes and no vegetation; a trace of snow only on the highest distant ridgeline.
